decisions.what: The M5 accept's poison is 're-apply tokens with the fontFace activation stripped', and both wp_verify calls in the driver are preceded by wp_disconnect (fresh session).
decisions.why: Deleting the wp_font_family post does not stop rendering — activation lives as embedded src urls in the user global-styles record (decision 14); and a warm session left over from an epoch-moving apply can be dead-but-cached, the recorded S9 discipline — the driver hung 9 minutes on wp_verify before adopting it.

decisions.what: Fixed en route (surfaced by the M3 accept): --until now binds RESUMED runs — a completed stage that is the --until target breaks the loop instead of continuing past it. Previously a resume of a run stopped at --until sailed into later stages (the M3 resume wandered into S3 and died on a missing fixture).
decisions.why: The until-check lived after the completed-skip `continue`; nothing before the theme factory ever resumed an --until run, so the latent bug had no witness. Pinned by a run.test.mjs regression.

decisions.what: Split-frame constants are code's: the frame is one align:full flex row, x-pane-primary fills, x-pane-secondary is fixed at 34%; an undeclared root (an S7 pattern baseline substituted late) lands in primary. Rail seam audits judge the footer against the MAIN ROW, never the column's last band (the flex row's bottom is whichever pane is tallest).
decisions.why: Pane widths and fallbacks are assembly, not authorship — same altitude as the rail width constant; and a rail taller or shorter than its column must not fake a footer seam.

decisions.what: Two M4 fixture clauses were reworded to what the geometry actually proves: pane bands are GRANDCHILDREN of post-content, so the stacked audit does not reject them — it cannot see them. The load-bearing property of the pane-aware audit is COVERAGE (a band clamped inside its pane, a seam inside a pane column — both invisible to the stacked audit, both caught by the split one), plus the arithmetic fact that a viewport expectation would reject every healthy pane-width band.
decisions.why: The spec imagined 'a viewport-width assertion would fail' the split fixture; structurally the old audit passes it blind. Asserting blindness + added coverage is the honest form of the same protection.

decisions.what: The themes/install route's returned fingerprint is BEST EFFORT and says so: a theme's init-time contributions (block style variations from theme.json partials and friends) only register on the NEXT request, and no cache bust re-runs init — measured live as a deterministic one-request epoch drift. The authoritative epoch is the post-install manifest refresh wp_theme_install performs; the live suite asserts the steady-state epoch moved and is stable, never in-request exactness.
decisions.why: The block installer could reregister() its ONE block in-request; a theme's init surface is unbounded, and simulating core's init would be a version-coupled lie. Two real cache bugs (WP_Theme cache serving a replaced copy's version; the per-theme global-styles resolver memo) were fixed on the way and are load-bearing.

decisions.what: The bespoke theme owns flush bands structurally: S3's SEAM_RESET selectors ride into theme.json styles.css byte-for-byte, so root block-gap seams measure zero at the build gate while blockGap stays declared for inner layout rhythm. S3's stage-authored reset remains as belt.
decisions.why: The spec's physics line: 'blockGap (declared, owned — the seam-reset apparatus becomes belt, not load-bearing)'. Zeroing global blockGap instead would collapse rhythm inside every layout; leaving the root gap live would fail the build gate's 'root block-gap seams zero'.

decisions.what: The build gate's wide-band expectation is pane-aware from birth: expected = min(declared wideSize, the content column's CONTENT box). Verified live — under the rail skeleton a wide band correctly clamps to the column (1048px of a 1440px viewport), and a border-box comparison was wrong by exactly the root padding.
decisions.why: 'Full means the pane the skeleton assigns, not the viewport' applies inside the sandbox too; the first live rail run failed on a viewport-shaped expectation, which is the same bug S9's pane-aware audit exists to prevent.

decisions.what: ThemeSpec.physics carries only what varies (blockGap, rootPadding); useRootPaddingAwareAlignments, appearanceTools and fluid typography are scaffolder constants, always on.
decisions.why: The theme carries only what a call cannot decide — a constant is code's to decide, and a model asked to author a constant is a model invited to vary it.

decisions.what: The measure sanity gate compares contentSize < wideSize only when the units match; mismatched units fail with 'use the same unit for both'.
decisions.why: px, ch and rem are not mechanically commensurable without a rendering context; a gate that guesses a conversion is a gate that lies.

decisions.what: theme-spec.schema.json is written strictly inside pipeline/lib/schema.mjs's draft-07 keyword subset, and the theme-spec test walks the schema refusing any unsupported keyword.
decisions.why: The subset validator silently ignores unknown keywords — a contract leaning on $ref or anyOf would be decorative, and a decorative gate is worse than none.
